memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom, saying: "This is what your brother Israel says: You know about all the hardships that have come on us. Our ancestors went down into Egypt, and we lived there many years. The Egyptians mistreated us and our ancestors, but when we cried out to the Lord, he heard our cry and sent an angel and brought us out of Egypt. Now we are here at Kadesh, a town on the edge of your territory." — Num 20:14-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Israel needed to pass through Edom's territory, and Moses handles it with wisdom and grace. He sends a respectful message, calling Edom "your brother Israel" — for the Edomites descended from Esau, Jacob's brother. Rather than forcing his way through, Moses seeks peaceful passage, appealing to their shared family history and telling honestly of Israel's hardships.

There is much to learn here about how to approach others, even those with whom our relationship is complicated. Moses is courteous, honest, and humble. He does not come with threats or arrogance but with respect. He acknowledges the kinship, recounts the truth plainly, and makes a reasonable request. This is the wisdom of seeking peace before conflict.

Scripture calls us to this same posture: "If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone." We cannot control how others respond, but we can control our own approach. We can choose courtesy over confrontation, humility over pride, honesty over manipulation. Making the first move toward peace is not weakness; it is the strength of a heart shaped by God.

This peacemaking spirit reflects the heart of our Saviour, who is called the Prince of Peace, and who came to reconcile us to God when we were His enemies. Jesus taught, "Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God." As those reconciled to God through Christ, we are now called to be agents of peace in a divided world. Whatever tensions you face, consider how you might make the first respectful move toward peace, as Moses did.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you tend to approach conflict with courtesy or with confrontation?
2. Where might God be calling you to make the first move toward peace?
3. How does being reconciled to God through Christ shape you as a peacemaker?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, help me to seek peace with others as far as it depends on me, approaching even difficult relationships with courtesy and humility. Thank You for reconciling me to Yourself through Christ. Make me a peacemaker in a divided world. Amen.
